rules.label: A first professionally qualifying university degree recognised in Germany, or a degree from a state-recognised vocational academy in computer science

check.note: TU Dresden decides whether your degree is recognised in Germany and fits computer science. A degree not yet awarded may be considered once 80% of its credits are achieved (certified by your university).

citations.quote: The prerequisite for admission to the course is a first professionally qualifying university degree recognized in Germany or a degree from a state or state-recognized vocational academy in computer science.

rules.label: English at CEFR C1: IELTS 7.0, TOEFL iBT 95 (or 5.0 on the new TOEFL scale), or another internationally offered C1 test

children.note: The page deems C1 proven by TOEFL iBT or IELTS 7.0 and asks for a C1 result 'based on an internationally offered test'; other tests at C1 may be accepted. The profile has no generic English level, so TU Dresden decides.

citations.quote: Proof of the required English language skills at level C 1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) based on the result of an internationally offered test.
Proof is deemed to have been provided if the “Test of English as a Foreign Language” TOEFL iBt (120-95) (New: 5.0 points) or the IELTS test was passed with at least level 7.0.

rules.label: TU Dresden aptitude assessment procedure (special aptitude for the Master's programme)

check.note: Admission needs a pass in the faculty's aptitude assessment under its regulations; no scoring formula is published, so it cannot be computed.

citations.quote: Proof of special aptitude is provided through aptitude assessment procedures in accordance with the Master Computer Science aptitude assessment regulations.

rules.label: APS certificate, for Chinese, Vietnamese or Indian educational certificates

citations.quote: Applicants with Chinese, Vietnamese or Indian educational certificates must submit a certificate from the Academic Evaluation Center (APS) with their application.

rules.label: With a foreign degree: apply by 15 July (EU nationals) or 31 May (non-EU nationals) for the winter term

Applicants with a foreign university degree

- Application period: EU applicants: 1st April – 15th July , 1st October – 15th January Non-EU applicants: 1st April – 31st May , 1st October – 30th November
